name: cover
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Create an original editorial cover illustration, landscape 3:2, no lettering at all. A small eccentric greenhouse engineering bench: a precisely tended miniature bonsai tree grows in a shallow dark green ceramic tray that is also a mechanical keyboard; its roots are visible below the tray as finely bundled wires being fitted into a fresh brass-and-wood support frame. Beside it sits the old empty support frame and a gardener's small hand tools. The living crown is intact while the support changes. Quiet intelligent natural-history-meets-computer-engineering metaphor about migrating an application's reactive UI framework without replacing its language. No human portraits, no drawers, no filing cabinet, no moth, no magnifying glass, no question-mark creature. Handmade underground literary zine, antique botanical engineering engraving with 1970s alternative-comic linework, crisp dark forest-black crosshatching, moss green and limited vermilion spot ink, warm ivory paper, restrained stamp texture and irregular hand-drawn edges, tangible fine print. Bold readable silhouette and an engaging close composition; do not make a busy poster or infographic. No lettering, numerals, labels, border, glossy gradients or photorealism.

name: cover
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Original conceptual editorial illustration for an underground programming zine. Landscape 3:2, absolutely no text or lettering. Close view of an old drafting table with a long paper program represented by coherent rows of small geometric marks and intentional empty cut-out slots, not actual readable code. Two instruments work on the same sheet: a human-sized fountain pen held by a striped fabric sleeve, and a small articulated brass drafting arm holding a vermilion pencil. The mechanical arm offers a precisely cut paper patch toward one empty slot; a tiny paper ladder beside the table suggests navigation. A second empty chair is drawn into the workstation. The scene is about an assistant joining an existing editing process, not replacing the author. Hands and machines are fictional abstractions, no developer portrait. Strong composition with paper, arm and empty slot central, atmospheric shadows made from crosshatching. Forest-black ink, moss green and sparse red on ivory, handmade woodcut/etching, alternative literary comic, slightly odd and quiet, rough printed texture but fine crisp detail. No robots with faces, no speech balloons, no trees, drawers, moths or repeated cover motifs. No title, borders, logos, photorealism or glossy 3D.

name: cover
prompt: Use case: illustration-story. Make an original landscape 3:2 editorial illustration, no words, letters, labels or numerals. In a slightly fantastical print workshop, two narrow feeds of translucent paper converge into one sturdy old forest-green printing press. One feed bears carefully aligned little geometric outlines; the other bears matching filled shapes. In the press the two layers align. The output is a generous accordion-folded sheet with elegant rows of geometric marks, precise red registration dots and small intentional gaps. Three distinct trays hold circular red stamps, triangular yellow tags and rectangular green slips, arranged neatly but not sterile. This is an indirect metaphor for combining type analysis and elaboration while giving diagnostic categories separate identities, and for good code layout. Fine engraved crosshatching, tactile black ink, restrained moss green, vermilion and pale ochre on warm ivory paper. Underground science/literary zine, vintage printmaking with hand-drawn irregularity and interesting machinery, beautiful detailed wide composition. No characters, tree, filing cabinet, moth, magnifying glass or repeated earlier zine iconography. No text, typography, border, logo, gradient or photorealism.
